tip_title: You Just Bought New Stuff for the Holidays. Your Policy Might Only Pay You What It's Worth Now — Not What It Costs to Replace It.
topic: Home Insurance - Personal Property ACV vs. Replacement Cost for Holiday Purchases
blurb:
💡 **Insurance Tip: Your Policy Has Two Ways to Value Your Belongings. One of Them Will Surprise You.**

Most homeowners policies cover the structure of your home at replacement cost — meaning if your roof gets destroyed, the insurer pays to rebuild it at today's prices. But your personal belongings (furniture, electronics, appliances, clothes) often default to actual cash value, which factors in depreciation. That five-year-old laptop that cost you $1,400 might pay out $400 at claim time. With the holiday shopping season starting now, it's worth pulling up your declarations page and finding out which method applies to your contents coverage before you bring new stuff through the door.

Not sure which settlement method you have on your policy? Your Peachy agent can look it up and walk you through what it means for your situation — takes about five minutes.

📖 [Learn more from the NAIC](https://content.naic.org/article/whats-difference-between-actual-cash-value-coverage-and-replacement-cost-coverage)
summary: Covers the ACV vs. replacement cost distinction for personal property contents coverage specifically framed around the holiday shopping season — new purchases entering the home make this a timely check on whether the contents settlement method is adequate.
scoring_notes: Prior ACV vs. replacement cost tips (July 6, Nov 6) covered the general distinction and the declarations-page check framing. This tip takes a fresh angle: the holiday purchase season as the trigger for checking contents settlement method specifically — new items coming into the home in November/December make this immediately concrete. High relevance across both audiences: East Cobb (78% homeowners, families making big holiday purchases) and Perimeter (55% homeowners but high education/income, also active shoppers). Actionability is strong — there's a specific thing to check right now. Timeliness is high given Thanksgiving week and Black Friday immediately ahead.
